title: The Ice Machine
setup: Word through the vent: the ice machine at {nearest_fuel} melted into a sealed bin. That's a lot of water, just sitting there.

options.label: Go with every jug you own
options.outcome: {name} makes two trips with sloshing jugs. Two bottles' worth, faintly flavoured like the inside of an ice machine.

options.label: Go after dark with one jug

effects.why: someone watched the jug go into the hatch

options.outcome: One jug, one quiet trip, and somebody on a porch watching the whole way.

options.label: Wait a few days for the dust to settle

then.text: Some of it is still there.

else.text: The bin is empty by the time anyone goes.

options.outcome: Three days later, {name} goes over with one jug and low expectations.

title: One Bag Per Family
setup: A note through the vent: {nearest_pharmacy} is handing out what's left at noon. One bag per family, while it lasts.

options.label: Queue from dawn
options.outcome: {name} is fourth in line by sunrise. The bag has bandages, antibiotics and a leaflet about flu season.

options.label: Go at noon and hope

then.text: The last bags are going as {name} arrives. One of them is theirs.

else.text: The bags ran out two people ahead of {name}.

options.outcome: {name} walks over at noon, into a queue that already goes round the corner.

options.label: Stay in; it isn't worth the dose
options.outcome: Nobody goes. Everyone spends the afternoon thinking about antibiotics.

title: Charging Station
setup: Someone has wheeled a generator out to the kerb by {nearest_hardware} and is charging phones. One can buys an hour.

options.label: Pay a can to charge every phone
options.outcome: No signal, but the photos still open. Everyone spends the evening scrolling through last summer. Forty-one updates install themselves.

options.label: Charge one phone for the offline maps

then.text: A cached alert has a fallout map in it, three days stale.

else.text: The maps need an update. The update needs a signal.

options.outcome: Half a can's worth buys half a charge. {name} watches the battery icon creep upward for an hour.

options.label: Keep the cans
options.outcome: The phones stay dark in a drawer. Somebody keeps opening the drawer to check anyway.

title: Lunches for Six Hundred
setup: A neighbour shouts through the vent: the cafeteria at {nearest_school} stocked lunches for six hundred. Nobody has been in yet.

options.label: Go tonight, before the street does

effects.why: someone saw the cans go into the hatch

options.outcome: {name} comes back at 2 a.m. with two cans of {food_label} and a crate of milk cartons nobody trusts.

options.label: Mark it for a proper trip

else.text: By the time the trip is planned, the street has been through the cafeteria.

options.outcome: It goes on the map in red pen, with a note: kitchen door, round the back.

title: Soup at Noon
setup: The bell at {nearest_church} rings at noon. A volunteer passing the vent says there's soup, one bowl each, no questions.

options.label: Everyone goes
options.outcome: The whole family walks over together for the first time since the flash. Hot soup, a long table, a short walk home.

options.label: Send one person with a pot
options.outcome: {name} carries the pot home with both hands, very slowly, as if it's full of something precious. It is.

options.label: Send two cans for the pot instead
options.outcome: Two cans go into the soup for whoever comes next. The volunteer adds the family to a thank-you list.

title: Household Return
setup: A volunteer from the station house has taped a form to the hatch: names, ages, supplies on hand. Block capitals, please.

options.label: Fill it in honestly

effects.why: someone read the household form on the hatch

options.outcome: Names, ages and an honest count of cans, in capitals. It stays taped to the hatch until collected, legible to anyone.

options.label: Round the supplies down

effects.why: someone read the household form on the hatch

options.outcome: Fewer cans on paper than on the shelf. {name} writes it very neatly, which somehow makes it worse.

options.label: Leave it blank

effects.text: A second copy of the household form appears on the hatch, stamped REMINDER.

options.outcome: Nobody fills it in. The household does not, officially, exist.

title: The Water Heater
setup: The water heater upstairs still holds a full tank. It has also spent a week in a house full of dust.

options.label: Drain it slowly and boil it
options.outcome: A whole day of draining, straining and boiling. One bottle, clean, and a kitchen that smells of rust.

options.label: Strain it through a T-shirt
options.outcome: Two bottles, faintly orange. The T-shirt will never be white again.

options.label: Drink it straight from the valve
options.outcome: Three bottles: all of it, rust and grit included. It tastes like the inside of a pipe.

title: Tracked In
setup: {subject} came down the ladder without brushing off. Grey dust is on the steps, the rug and the blankets.

options.label: Wash everything with drinking water
options.outcome: Three rations of water, a lot of scrubbing, and a very clean rug. Nobody steps on the rug for a day.

options.label: Bag the blankets and take them upstairs
options.outcome: The blankets go up the ladder in bin bags. The nights get longer and colder.

options.label: Shake it off and carry on

then.why: fallout dust tracked into the shelter

options.outcome: A quick shake at the ladder and a sweep under the rug. The dust is still there, just better organised.

title: Insurance Policy
setup: {subject} suggests burying two cans in the garden, in case the shelter is ever raided. It's not a bad idea, which is unsettling.

options.label: Bury two cans under the roses
options.outcome: Two cans of {food_label}, double-bagged, under the roses. {subject} marks the spot with a stick and a long stare.

options.label: Keep everything where you can see it
options.outcome: The cans stay on the shelf where everyone can count them. Everyone does, twice a day.

title: Under the Roses
setup: Six nights on, the garden looks different in the dark. Somebody has to remember which stick was the stick.

options.label: Dig them up tonight

then.text: Both cans, a little muddy, entirely intact.

else.text: One can. Something with whiskers dug up the other.

options.outcome: {name} digs by feel under three wrong sticks before finding the right one.

options.label: Dig in daylight, where you can see

effects.why: a neighbour watched someone dig cans out of the garden

options.outcome: Right stick, first try, both cans. It takes twenty minutes in the open, and the house across the road has curtains that move.

title: Out for Delivery
setup: A courier is still working his route on foot. He has a parcel for next door and asks if you'll sign for it.

options.label: Sign for it
options.outcome: {name} signs with a fingertip on a cracked screen. The parcel is heavy and rattles. The courier asks for five stars.

options.label: Sign for it, then open it

then.text: A camping torch, still in the box, batteries included.

else.text: It's a smart toaster. It wants a network and a firmware update.

options.outcome: {name} signs, waits for the courier to turn the corner, and opens it on the steps.

options.label: Decline the delivery
options.outcome: He marks it ATTEMPTED and walks on. He has fourteen more stops and no van.

title: Any Parcels for Me?
setup: The neighbour from next door is at the hatch. The tracking said delivered. They'd like their parcel.

options.label: Hand it over

then.text: It was water filters and a bottle. They insist on leaving the bottle.

options.outcome: They open it right there on the step. Everyone pretends not to look.

options.label: Say it never came
options.outcome: They nod slowly and go. The parcel turns out to be a first-aid kit, which doesn't help as much as it should.

title: Many Happy Returns
setup: It's {subject}'s birthday. Nobody planned for it, least of all {subject}.

options.label: Make a cake out of a can of {food_label}
options.outcome: It's a cake in the sense that it has a candle in it. {subject} blows it out and makes a wish nobody asks about.

options.label: Sing, loudly

effects.why: the singing carried up the vent

options.outcome: Three verses, two keys, one very red face. The singing carries further up the vent than anyone meant it to.

options.label: Promise a proper party later

effects.text: Somebody remembers the promised birthday party. It is still promised.

options.outcome: {subject} says it's fine, the way people say fine when it isn't, quite.

title: Emergency Alert
setup: Every phone in the shelter buzzes at once. EMERGENCY ALERT: possible nuclear event in your area. It's day {day}.

options.label: Write a strongly worded complaint
options.outcome: Four pages, double-sided, addressed To Whom It May Concern. It concerns nobody. Morale is briefly excellent.

options.label: Climb up for one bar and read the rest

then.text: A second alert follows, with a fallout map. It's only slightly late.

else.text: The rest of the alert is a link. The link needs a signal.

options.outcome: {name} stands on the hatch, holding a phone up at the sky until the bar comes back.

options.label: Turn every phone off for good
options.outcome: One by one, the screens go dark and go in a drawer. The group chat ends on a thumbs-up.

title: Short Back and Sides
setup: {subject} has found the kitchen scissors and is offering haircuts. They watched a lot of tutorials, once.

options.label: Everybody lines up
options.outcome: Everyone gets the same haircut, which is a choice. One fringe will take a month to forgive.

options.label: {name} goes first, alone
options.outcome: {name} sits very still for forty minutes. The result is described, generously, as practical.

options.label: Hide the scissors
options.outcome: The scissors go on the top shelf. {subject} sulks with the air of an artist who has been censored.

title: One Cup
setup: {subject} is running a fever, and the whole family has been drinking from the same cup since day two.

options.label: Give {subject} their own cup and a corner

then.why: caught it from the shared cup

options.outcome: {subject} gets a cup with their name on it in marker, and a corner behind the shelves. It's lonely back there.

options.label: Boil the cup after every sip
options.outcome: {name} boils the cup so often it starts to look nervous. Two rations of water go up as steam.

options.label: Keep sharing; it's only a cold

then.why: caught it from the shared cup

options.outcome: It's only a cold, everyone agrees, passing the cup.
